what: PX-3 (2026-10-20): the step program's choices taken per site from measured candidates -- every kind of choice site (the q/k/v and gate/up projections' grouping, the SwiGLU panels, the down, o, gate/up and q/k/v VJPs' grouping, the head's VJP) measured in place by the job clock on one trainer in rotated rounds, the frozen ChoiceTable that results, the choice it makes, and the chosen program, the default and the program the measurement prices slowest run end to end at the same state -- on the 9.84M comparison decoder (vocabulary 260, width 384, 8 heads over 4 KV heads, 6 layers, FF 1024, tied; 8 sequences of 128 tokens).

reading: On the 9.84M comparison decoder at four threads (this host: AVX-512F, neither AMX nor AVX512-BF16), under bf16 every one of the ten alternatives reads slower at its sites than the step's default, each interval wholly above 1.0: a call each for the q/k/v and gate/up projections x1.094 and x1.047, the SwiGLU block plain x1.074, a call each for the down, o, gate/up, q/k/v and head VJPs x1.055, x1.039, x1.078, x1.156 and x1.062, a job a projection for the gate/up and q/k/v VJPs x1.035 and x1.102: NDT-SCHED-0/1's grouping and pairing and BF16-PANELS' panels are the measured winners at every site. Under binary32 none of the nine reads either way (x0.965 to x1.070, every interval holding 1.0). So `choose` keeps the defaults under both. End to end, in 32 rounds of four trainers of the library without the clock, the program the measurement prices slowest (every kind at its slowest alternative: 893 launches a four-step call against the default's 577) runs x1.0641 (95% interval 1.043-1.086) of the default under bf16, slower in 29 of 32 rounds, where its readings predicted x1.096 for the jobs it switches; under binary32 it reads x0.9995 (0.975-1.025), its readings having predicted x1.017. The chosen program is the default's, so its arm is a third trainer running the default program: x0.983 and x0.966 against the first, beside the A/A control's x0.983 and x0.990. Trainers running one program differ by up to 3.4% on this host, an offset the rounds' interval does not hold -- which is why the choice rests on one trainer's readings in place; the slowest program's x1.064 under bf16 lies beyond it (x1.083 against each of the other two). Every trainer's state is one state, bit for bit. The measurement took 458 s under bf16 and 235 s under binary32 (24 rotated rounds of four-step calls on one trainer of the clocked library); the table, its raw readings round by round and the end-to-end milliseconds are in each record.
